A: A pair of fine links carries both a retained product and a free midpoint. Once all coarse products are fixed, the remaining link variables form a compact manifold. Dividing by gauge transformations at eliminated vertices gives the quotient on which the conditional energy is defined. The conditional law needs a canonical version if an inequality is claimed at every coarse field. The cut introduces a further geometric issue. A.7 exhibits a quotient geodesic leaving the cut between two admissible endpoints.
B: Conditioning a Gaussian changes the subspace on which its precision acts. A fixed-fibre gap, the joint conditionally centred gap and the physical colour-singlet gap therefore answer different variational questions. Hermite degrees add exactly on a fixed fibre. On the joint space conditioning mixes the retained and eliminated directions inside a degree. A two-mode calculation exposes the difference before the open-cube computations quantify it.
C: Free gaps in open and periodic boxes

A fine one-cochain is a function on oriented links. Its circulation around a plaquette is a discrete curl. A path argument controls the norm of an eliminated transverse cochain by this curl and supplies a lower bound independent of side length. Fourier aliases then give a much sharper answer for periodic scalar problems. Open physical boxes enter the master claim and have their own boundary question.
D: The conditional density is built from a Hamiltonian ground state. Its logarithmic Hessian measures the confinement of the eliminated variables. Three analytic approaches and one mixing alternative isolate the estimates that remain missing at arbitrary volume. One pinned SU(2) link admits a direct curvature argument on the full weak interval, giving a test of the mechanism in an interacting finite model.
E: Consequences of a uniform curvature floor

A conditional premise is valuable only if its constants survive each step to the physical bound. Starting with the curvature and cut-domain hypotheses, this unit follows the same constant through variance, energy, entropy and scale separation. The final assembly also consumes retained transport and mixed Schur bounds from W2.
F: Upper variational trials, confidence intervals, rigorous interval enclosures and Lean proofs give different information. This unit computes finite-model benchmarks and documents how to reproduce each kind of evidence. A public release and an author-hosted Lean check have independent provenance.
